Terrain-adaptive exoskeleton

I designed and built a lower-extremity exoskeleton to explore terrain-aware gait assistance, from sensing and prediction to hardware control.

My role: design, ML, and hardware integrationRegeneron ISEF finalist · 2024

The prototype in motion

40-second demo of the supported, bench-mounted prototype. The footage demonstrates joint motion; it does not establish performance during human walking.

Sensing, prediction, control

I combined IMU and RGB-D sensor fusion, real-time terrain classification using PointNet++, gait prediction models, and high-torque servo control.

  1. Sense

    IMU and RGB-D inputs provide motion and terrain information.

  2. Interpret

    PointNet++ classifies terrain. Gait prediction models inform the control system.

  3. Actuate

    High-torque servos drive the prototype’s leg joints.

Tracking the movement

The sequence documents motion. It is not a measurement of tracking error or evidence of terrain-classification accuracy.

Hardware & build

The project included the physical build and electronics integration as well as the models.
